newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National Mutual NZ gen manager Ractliffe to quit.
newsitem.headline: National Mutual NZ gen manager Ractliffe to quit.

text.p: In a surprise move, National Mutual's New Zealand general manager Anthony Ractliffe is to quit the company after 30 years' service, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Wednesday.
Ractliffe will leave National Mutual in November, only a month after the company lists on the Stock Exchange.
Ractliffe, 55, has been based in Wellington for the past seven years and was to return to National Mutual's headquarters in Melbourne once the listing assignment was completed.
Yesterday, Ractliffe said he and his wife Diana had decided to live in New Zealand, particularly Wellington, rather than return to Melbourne.
British born but raised in Capetown, he and his family had not lived in any other city for more than four years in a globe-trotting lifestyle lasting 30 years.

"This is the longest we've ever stayed in one place and to stay here has meant I have to leave National Mutual. It has been very amicable and I am to stay on as an independent director of one of National Mutual's subsidiaries, NZ Permanent Trustees," he said.
Ractliffe said he was considering his options, including several directorships. He did not plan to seek work as a chief executive for another company.
"I must confess, with the extraordinary amount of work we have had to take on prior to the listing, I have virtually given no time to my own personal position."
